primitives.name: Social Signal to Inference Pipeline
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Sweep method per account:** profile (bio, counts, website) → recent posts (captions, claims, engagement) → chase every public lead (repo README + license via GitHub API, public docs, papers) → extract kernel → verdict.
primitives.assumptions: All data is publicly accessible and non-sensitive; leads are semantically traceable to source repositories or documentation.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When public leads are absent or ambiguous, fallback to engagement-based heuristics.

layer2.mapping: Each social post maps to a probabilistic claim-space where kernel metrics define evidence weight and veracity score.
layer2.telemetry: Engagement rate, lead-follow-through ratio, and kernel reuse frequency.

primitives.name: Derived Computer Vision Metrics
primitives.verbatim_quote: Kernel: breakAngle / sepAtBreak / sepAtCatch as derived CV metrics → WR route-quality → props.
primitives.assumptions: Player tracking data is available in video frames; metrics are extracted via pose estimation models.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When pose estimation fails or tracking is occluded, metrics default to zero or interpolated values.

layer2.mapping: CV-derived kinematic features encode route quality and prop-value potential in real-time.
layer2.telemetry: Pose estimation confidence, frame-rate consistency, and feature drift across clips.

primitives.name: Contrarian Hook Extraction
primitives.verbatim_quote: Kernels to steal: daily cadence, trends-carousel containers, comment-gated magnets, data-compatible contrarian hooks.
primitives.assumptions: Contrarian framing is detectable via linguistic and behavioral patterns in content distribution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When hooks are too generic or lack data alignment, they are flagged for low utility.

layer2.mapping: Contrarian hooks are modeled as probabilistic incentives that drive engagement and data compatibility.
layer2.telemetry: Comment-gating success rate, carousel click-through, and hook-to-data alignment score.

This process involves extracting semantic kernels—such as derived computer vision metrics or contrarian framing—that act as proxies for deeper truths. These kernels are then evaluated under a Bayesian framework where prior beliefs about signal reliability are updated based on observed engagement and data compatibility. The failure mode occurs when signals lack sufficient grounding in public data or when kernels are misapplied due to incorrect assumptions about data structure or model validity. Dualities emerge between signal strength and kernel fidelity, where strong signals may still fail if their underlying kernels are misaligned with real-world dynamics.
